source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry — this sounds great, I like the approach and timeline.

Let’s move forward.

For the first step, I’d like to focus on:
• system layout
• motor + component selection
• basic wiring plan

Goal is to get a working prototype up and running as quickly as possible, then refine from there.

Let me know what you need from me to get started.

value_updates.selection_goal: support rapid construction of the initial working prototype

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: I've got the initial BOM ready for you to look at, taking into consideration the recent design elements you mentioned. Some parts, Such as any additional wires, hardware and housing which will be custom fabricated, I already have the material for these my shop and they will be added to the BOM in the future once the build begins. I'll now begin the initial cad design using rough measurements of the components. This will be refined once you approve the components and the purchasing of them so that accurate measurements of each piece can be taken by me to refine the design fully. I've stuck to amazon for all the components so that we can quickly iterate if something needs to be changed or added in the future.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry — I went through the finalized BOM and everything is looking really solid. I like the direction a lot and I think we’re very close to locking this in.

I just had a few quick things I wanted to confirm before I move forward with ordering parts:

• Motors — I noticed the listing mentions an eccentric output shaft. Just want to confirm that this will still give us a smooth, centered rotation for the whisk, or if we should consider a straight/centered shaft for better stability.

• Motor performance — I like the move to 3000 RPM for flexibility. I just want to make sure we’ll be able to dial it in for smooth mixing and avoid overly aggressive splashing at higher speeds.

• Solenoid flow — since we’re using on/off valves, do you expect the pour to be smooth when opening, or will it release too abruptly? I want to make sure we get a clean, controlled pour without splashing.

• Power supply — with both motors, solenoids, and fans running, are we comfortably within the limits of the 12V 20A power supply under load?

• Splash control — with the higher RPM, I just want to confirm that whisk positioning, bowl depth, and overall layout will keep things clean during operation. I want this to be as splash-proof and mess-free as possible for events.

Everything else looks great to me — just want to make sure we’re fully dialed in on these before the order is placed.

Let me know your thoughts.

pre_order_compatibility_checks: motor shaft and coupling selection must support smooth centered whisk rotation
electrical component ratings must support both motors, solenoids, and fans under load

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: Newly updated BOM. Only difference between this one and the previous is that the PWM motor controllers have been swapped out for higher power ones. And the AC/DC adapter has been swapped out for a 50A version which should supply more than enough power with reserves to ensure nothing overheats. I also went through and confirmed pricing on everything as there was a few discrepancies in the prices I had listed and the current prices.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports updating the BOM with higher-power PWM controllers, a 50A power supply, and corrected pricing.
